- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

Findings below. All paths absolute.

## Q1 — Handlers that can trigger an outbound webhook HTTP request

### Convergence point (the single function where all paths meet before HTTP delivery)

- `webhook.Post` — `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:120`, with the actual outbound call at `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:152` (`safeClient.Do(req)`).
- Every API path reaches it *asynchronously* via `webhook.PostAsync` — `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:184`, which enqueues onto `asyncPostQueue` (`/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:39`); four init-time worker goroutines drain the queue and call `Post` at `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:46`.
- So: if you want the single funnel *inside the request goroutine*, it is `(*APIV1Service).dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook` — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:48` (dispatch at line 71). The comment path bypasses it and calls `PostAsync` directly at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:43`. The true universal funnel for HTTP delivery is `webhook.Post` / line 152.

### Dispatch wrappers

- `DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook` — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:15`
- `DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook` — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:20`
- `DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook` — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:25`
- `DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook` — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:30`

### Handler methods that transitively reach it (5 total)

1. `CreateMemo` — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:70`; dispatch at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:157` (`DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook`).
2. `UpdateMemo` — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:401`; calls `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:513` → `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_update_helpers.go:67`.
3. `DeleteMemo` — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:518`; dispatch at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:562` (`DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook`), fired *before* the rows are deleted.
4. `SetMemoAttachments` — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go:16`; `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go:48`.
5. `SetMemoRelations` — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_relation_service.go:16`; `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_relation_service.go:48`.
6. `CreateMemoComment` — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:20`; dispatch at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:119`. Note this one dispatches to the **parent memo owner's** webhooks (`relatedMemo.CreatorID`), i.e. a commenter can cause an outbound request to a URL configured by a *different* user.

Negative result worth stating: `UpsertMemoReaction` (`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go:60`) and `DeleteMemoReaction` (`:111`) do **not** reach the webhook layer — they only broadcast SSE (`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go:106`). Same for attachment upload in `attachment_service.go`.

### Transport-edge notes

- Public entrypoints are the Connect wrappers: `CreateMemo` `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/connect_services.go:306`, `UpdateMemo` `:330`, `DeleteMemo` `:338`, `SetMemoAttachments` `:346`, `SetMemoRelations` `:362`, `CreateMemoComment` `:378`.
- The MCP router is an additional reachability edge: `/bench/repo/server/router/mcp/adapter.go:34` re-enters `echoServer.ServeHTTP` with a synthesized request, and `MemoService_CreateMemo` / `MemoService_CreateMemoComment` are in the exposed tool catalog (`/bench/repo/server/router/mcp/catalog.go:13` and `:18`). So an MCP tool call also reaches `webhook.Post`.
- SSRF defenses exist at two layers: write-time `webhook.ValidateURL` (`/bench/repo/internal/webhook/validate.go:62`, called from `CreateUserWebhook` `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go:74` and `UpdateUserWebhook` `:161`/`:182`) and dial-time `safeDialContext` (`/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:59`, reserved-IP check at line 71), which is the DNS-rebinding-resistant one. `AllowPrivateIPs` (`/bench/repo/internal/webhook/validate.go:38`) can disable the check.

## Q2 — Avatar request → stored data

Route: `GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar`.

| # | Symbol | Location |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `FileServerService` constructed and routes mounted | `/bench/repo/server/server.go:81-82` |
| 1 | `(*FileServerService).RegisterRoutes` — registers the avatar route | `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:124` |
| 2 | `(*FileServerService).serveUserAvatar` — the handler | `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168` |
| 2a | anonymous gate: `s.Profile.AllowAnonymous()` | `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:173` → `/bench/repo/internal/profile/profile.go:46` (true iff `InstanceURL` is non-empty) |
| 2b | `(*FileServerService).getCurrentUser` (only when not anonymous-allowed) | `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:708` → `(*Authenticator).AuthenticateToUser` `/bench/repo/server/auth/authenticator.go:190` |
| 3 | `identifier := c.Param("identifier")` — raw, attacker-chosen username | `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:183` |
| 4 | `(*FileServerService).getUserByUsername` | `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715` — body is `s.Store.GetUser(ctx, &store.FindUser{Username: &identifier})` |
| 5 | `(*Store).GetUser` — checks `userCache` only on ID lookups, otherwise falls through | `/bench/repo/store/user.go:148` |
| 6 | `(*Store).ListUsers` — populates `userCache` for each row | `/bench/repo/store/user.go:136` (driver call at line 137) |
| 7 | `Driver.ListUsers` interface | `/bench/repo/store/driver.go:47` |
| 8 | `(*DB).ListUsers` per backend | sqlite `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/user.go:88`, postgres `/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/user.go:87`, mysql `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/user.go:84` |
| 8a | username predicate (parameterized) | `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/user.go:128-130` |
| 8b | SQL select including `avatar_url`, executed | `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/user.go:151-165`, `QueryContext` at `:173` |
| 8c | row scan into `user.AvatarURL` | `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/user.go:189` |
| 9 | back in handler: `(*FileServerService).parseDataURI` decodes the stored `data:` URI | `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:737`, regex at `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:98` |
| 10 | MIME allowlist `avatarAllowedTypes` then `c.Blob` response | `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:75`, check at `:201`, headers `:205-207`, body `:209` |

Observations on this path:

- Avatars are stored inline in the `user` row as a base64 `data:` URI (column `avatar_url`), not in the attachment/blob store — so "reaching stored data" is a single user-table read, no object storage hop.
- The only authorization on the path is the instance-wide anonymous gate at `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:173`. Once a viewer is authenticated (or the instance sets `InstanceURL`), **any** user's avatar is readable by username enumeration; there is no per-user visibility check, in contrast to attachments which go through `checkAttachmentPermission` (`/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:149`).
- Serving is defense-in-depth'd on write too: `UpdateUser` validates the avatar MIME on the `avatar_url` update mask at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service.go:335-350`, and the read path re-validates against `avatarAllowedTypes`, so a legacy/SSO-set `text/html` data URI cannot be served as HTML. SSO can set `AvatarURL` without that grpc validation at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go:64`, which makes the read-path check load-bearing.
- `/memos.api.v1.UserService/GetUserAvatar` is listed as an unauthenticated-allowed method at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/acl_config.go:25`, but no Go implementation of `GetUserAvatar` exists in the repo (only that ACL entry) — a stale allowlist entry.
